declared_families: peer-reviewed status, coalition, representation, and racial-order research
official oversight, appointment, procurement, and judicial records

records.title: The trainwreck is a vertical coalition, not a flat one
normalized_fact_record: Names a status-for-sovereignty compact organized as a vertical coalition with nested superiority.
Proposes conditional multiracial incorporation, allocator transfer, preference monopoly, counterfactual foreclosure, and distributed counterpower aversion.
Defines Question 4 as the practical test of standing, evidence, pause, correction, substitution, exit, and value recovery.
limitations: Structural synthesis and field hypothesis, not an independently verified empirical denominator.
Cannot establish the secret intent of voters, founders, investors, officials, or institutions.
Original attachment bytes are not preserved; the repository stores a bounded transcription.

records.title: The Symbolic Politics of Status in the MAGA Movement
records.publisher: Perspectives on Politics, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Analyzes MAGA as a status movement centered on lost honor, declining esteem, and perceived institutional disrespect.
Records belonging, pride, anger, and joy alongside grievance and policy preference.
Supplies a bounded status-motive mechanism rather than a national electorate denominator.
limitations: Ethnography does not establish every supporter’s motive.
No exact gate or consequence chain is supplied.
Status grievance alone does not establish racial hierarchy.

records.title: Embracing the Status Hierarchy: How Immigration Attitudes, Prejudice, and Sexism Shaped Non-White Support for Trump
records.publisher: Perspectives on Politics, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Across multiple datasets, hierarchy-related attitudes are associated with Trump support among Black, Latino, and Asian respondents.
Hierarchy-supporting attitudes are not unique to White respondents.
The association supports coalition heterogeneity without establishing individual motive or institutional order.
limitations: Associations do not establish every voter’s motive.
No institutional selection and remedy denominator is supplied.
Non-White support proves neither neutrality nor tokenism.

records.title: Detailed demographic profiles of Trump and Harris voters in 2024
normalized_fact_record: Pew reports that 78 percent of Trump’s 2024 voters were non-Hispanic White.
About one-fifth of Trump’s 2024 coalition was Hispanic, Black, Asian, or another race.
Composition establishes a genuinely multiracial coalition but not its governing structure or effects.
limitations: Composition cannot identify individual motive.
Diversity does not establish neutrality or justice.
No exact selector, consequence, or remedy is identified.

records.title: Racial Presence versus Racial Justice
records.publisher: Du Bois Review, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Distinguishes racial presence in elite institutions from racial justice.
Treats a racially diverse elite as politically indeterminate without authority and outcome evidence.
Supplies a falsifier against using representation alone as proof of neutrality or hierarchy.
limitations: Does not establish that a represented person lacks authority.
Does not prove tokenism in a specific institution.
Complete authority, outcome, and remedy records remain required.

records.title: Racial Orders in American Political Development
records.publisher: American Political Science Review, Cambridge University Press
normalized_fact_record: Develops a framework for competing racial institutional orders.
Treats racial order as an evolving constellation of institutions, practices, rules, and ideas rather than identical explicit beliefs.
Supplies vocabulary for testing institutional reproduction, not proof of a current order.
limitations: General framework does not classify a current institution.
No Wave 02 causal join is supplied.
No prevalence finding follows from framework fit.

records.title: EC259 — The Termination of Certain Inspector Generals
normalized_fact_record: Records a presidential message terminating inspectors general across sixteen named departments, agencies, and offices.
Identifies the action as transmitted pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 403(b).
Establishes the dated removal instrument and affected offices, not motive or downstream effect.
limitations: Does not establish every affected investigation.
Does not establish motive or final legal resolution.
Removal authority does not settle procedural compliance.

records.title: Removal of Inspectors General: Rules, Practice, and Considerations for Congress
normalized_fact_record: Describes inspector general independence as central to statutory oversight.
Identifies a 30-day advance-notice requirement, substantive rationale, and restrictions on non-duty status.
States that the January 2025 action did not appear to follow notice and waiting requirements.
limitations: CRS is not a final judicial judgment.
Does not establish every removed official’s merits.
Procedural noncompliance alone does not establish the compact.

records.title: U.S. Senate Roll Call Vote 119th Congress — Vote 139
normalized_fact_record: The Senate confirmed Michael Kratsios as OSTP Director on March 25, 2025.
The recorded vote was 74 yeas and 25 nays.
The vote establishes public office and confirmation surface, not policy translation.
limitations: Confirmation does not establish later policy causation.
Does not establish coordination or common purpose.
Prior employment cannot be inferred from this record.

records.title: ICYMI: President Trump Outlines OSTP's Goals and Priorities
normalized_fact_record: Identifies Michael Kratsios as Assistant to the President and OSTP Director.
States goals covering critical technologies, the science enterprise, and economic and public benefit.
Establishes a policy surface but not which private artifact or relationship caused a public action.
limitations: Public agenda does not establish import from a private network.
No complete participant or outcome denominator.
Similarity of language is not causation.

records.title: Palantir USG, Inc., B-412746
normalized_fact_record: Palantir challenged the Army’s DCGS-A2 solicitation regarding commercial-item preference and competition.
GAO denied the protest after reviewing the solicitation and market-research record.
The decision establishes an alternative architecture claim and review, not later foreclosure.
limitations: Does not establish technical superiority.
No complete later support and performance denominator.
Denial does not establish improper selection.

records.title: General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc., B-416181
normalized_fact_record: General Dynamics protested rejection of its proposal under an Army DCGS-A solicitation.
GAO denied the protest after reviewing the demonstration and technical evaluation; Raytheon and Palantir were intervenors.
The decision confirms multiple participants and review while leaving support and counterfactual denominators unresolved.
limitations: Does not establish absence of structural advantage.
No comparable-data or long-run performance denominator.
Selected-vendor success cannot settle foreclosure.

records.title: Ames v. Ohio Department of Youth Services, slip opinion — repository reuse
records.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
normalized_fact_record: The unanimous Court rejected a heightened evidentiary burden for majority-group Title VII plaintiffs.
The Court vacated the judgment and remanded for the proper standard.
Supplies a bounded control in which an independent institution corrected an evidentiary rule without deciding the merits.
limitations: Does not decide whether Ames experienced discrimination.
Does not validate categorical anti-DEI enforcement.
One correction does not establish system-wide remedy effectiveness.

records.title: Docket 23-1039, Ames v. Ohio Department of Youth Services — repository reuse
records.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
normalized_fact_record: Records grant, argument, decision, vacatur, remand, and judgment issuance.
Preserves the procedural sequence for the bounded correction control.
Docket metadata does not establish the merits on remand.
limitations: Does not establish final merits.
Does not establish correction elsewhere.
Reuses canonical records rather than claiming new byte custody.
